# Q3 Planning Sync — 2026-08-27

**Attendees:** Priya (PM), Marcus (Eng lead), Jenna (Ops), Dan (Design), Sara (VP Product)

## Key decisions

- **Reconciliation revamp is the Q3 anchor.** Build wins over buy. The current engine fails on multi-currency batches (three incidents this quarter, reconciliation support tickets up 40% QoQ). Rewrite scoped at ~6 engineer-weeks, including migration of the FX rounding module. Vendors evaluated and rejected: Recur ($180K/yr) and LedgerFlow ($140K/yr, doesn't handle jurisdiction-specific tax codes); both would still need ~3 engineer-weeks of integration work.
- **Mobile receipt-capture ships v1 without bulk-select.** User testing (6 users) surfaced two asks: bulk-select before upload and a more prominent OCR confidence indicator. Bulk-select is roughly a sprint of work and would require descoping something else, so it goes on the roadmap as a fast-follow.
- **Vendor payout 48h SLA is not yet committed.** Finance wants payouts within 48 hours of invoice approval; current p95 is 71 hours. Proposed plan: eng cuts the ACH batching window from 12 hours to 4, ops adds a second approver on the west-coast shift, target 48h p95 by mid-Q3. Decision deferred pending a trade-off analysis (more ACH files per day, added monitoring overhead, ~half a sprint of eng time, SRE sign-off). If SRE says monitoring load is manageable, proceed; otherwise look at intermediate targets.
- **Audit-log retention update pushed to Q4**, confirmed with Legal.
- **Internal admin-tool refresh** stays with the intern crew; no changes.
- **On-call rotation:** HR flagged a spike in bug-bash burnout on the engineering side; Marcus to propose a rotating on-call structure (lightweight proposal, not a full program).

| Marcus | ACH batching trade-off analysis, including SRE sign-off on monitoring load | Next week |

| All | Q3 scope lock | Friday |
